title: Chapter 98 — Research Intelligence
intro: Using AI for competitive research, market intelligence, and product knowledge that gives you an edge.

sections.title: Competitive Research
sections.content:
Before every manufacturer training, before every trade show, and before every new product launch on your floor, use AI to do advance research. What is the competitive landscape? How does this new model compare to what is already on the floor? What are the selling angles the manufacturer will push — and what are the honest trade-offs they will not mention?

AI can synthesize product reviews, manufacturer spec sheets, and competitive comparisons in minutes. Use that synthesis to walk into training already informed — and to ask the questions that make you the most knowledgeable rep in the room.

sections.title: Market Intelligence
sections.content:
Use AI to track market trends relevant to your selling: which categories are growing, which brands are gaining or losing share, what design trends are emerging, and what technology shifts are coming.

This intelligence informs your prospecting, your product recommendations, and your conversations with trade accounts. The rep who says 'induction adoption is up 35 percent this year — are your clients asking about it?' sounds like a market expert, not a salesperson.

sections.title: Customer-Ready Research
sections.content:
When a customer asks about a brand or product you have not sold before, use AI to get smart in 5 minutes. Brand story, competitive positioning, common customer feedback, warranty structure, and the three selling angles that matter most.

This is not about faking expertise. It is about being able to engage intelligently with any customer question and then verifying the specifics before making a recommendation. The customer who asks about La Cornue ranges should not hear 'I am not familiar with that brand.' They should hear 'La Cornue is a French manufacturer with over 100 years of heritage. Let me pull up the specific model you are looking at.'
